identificationModule.briefTitle: Effects of Different Positions on Mechanical Traction Outcome
identificationModule.officialTitle: Effect of Different Positions During Traction on Pain, Function, and Range of Motion in Adults with Non-specific Low Back Pain

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Our primary purpose for this study is to investigate the effect of different positions during traction on pain, function, and range of motion in adults with non-specific low back pain.

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: It will be a triple-armed Randomized control trial, 30 subject will be recruited and randomly allocated into the three groups (supine, prone, and side-lying) using sealed envelope method, same treatment will be delivered with difference in positioning only, Supine Participants will lie in supine position with legs supported on a stool adjusted for hip and knee flexion to be at 90°, Prone Participants will lie in prone position with a pillow underneath their abdomen and a harness attached to the chest, and pelvis. Side-lying Participants will lie on the contralateral side of pain, with his hip flexed at 80°, and a pillow between his knees.

armGroups.label: Supine Participants
armGroups.description: Participants will lie in supine position with legs supported on a stool adjusted for hip and knee flexion to be at 90°

armGroups.label: Prone Participants
armGroups.description: will lie in prone position with a pillow underneath their abdomen and a harness attached to the chest, and pelvis

armGroups.label: Side-lying Participants
armGroups.description: will lie on the contralateral side of pain, with his hip flexed at 80°, and a pillow between their knees

interventions.name: mechanical traction
interventions.description: Participants will receive traction therapy as follows: force will start at 25% of Body weight, gradually increasing until the tolerance for pulling is reached with maximum of 50% of body weight. The session will be 15 minutes long (1min for acceleration, 13 min application, 1min deceleration); it will be intermittent with ratio of 30 s on and 10s off

primaryOutcomes.description: assesses the impact of back pain on daily life across 10 sections. Each section covers different activities and aspects of daily living. The responses are scored from 0 (no impact) to 5 (maximum impact), with higher scores indicating greater disability
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: from baseline to the end of the 6th week

secondaryOutcomes.measure: International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) arabic version
secondaryOutcomes.description: the questionnaire includes questions about various domains of activity, such as job-related activity, transportation, housework, and leisure-time physical activity
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: from baseline to the end of the 6th week

secondaryOutcomes.description: An 11-point scale that start at 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable pain)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: from baseline to the end of the 6th week

secondaryOutcomes.description: Participants will be asked to bend forward as much as possible, the distance between the tip of the middle finger and the platform is measured in Cm using a measurement tape.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: from baseline to the end of the 6th week

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult 18-65 years of age
* Non specific LBP persisted for more than 12 weeks
* At least 4/10 on NPRS

Exclusion Criteria:

* Vertebral fractures
* Axial spondylarthritis
* Aauda equina syndrome
* Radicular pain
* Radiculopathy
* Spinal stenosis
* Spinal surgeries
* Malignancy
* Pregnancy
* Inflammatory or infectious cases of LBP
